questions.question: Q2. If p is the perpendicular from origin to x/a+y/b = 1, prove 1/a^2+1/b^2 = 1/p^2.
questions.solution: p = |0+0-1|/√(1/a²+1/b²) = 1/√(1/a²+1/b²). So 1/a²+1/b² = 1/p². ∎ (proof-type; no key answer needed).

questions.question: Q4(a). Bisectors between 3x-4y+2 = 0 and 5x+12y+5 = 0.
questions.solution: (3x-4y+2)/5 = ±(5x+12y+5)/13: 13(3x-4y+2) = ±5(5x+12y+5). Branches: 14x-112y+1 = 0 and 64x+8y+51 = 0. (Each verified; consistent with the key family.)

questions.question: Q5(a). Bisectors of y = x and y = 7x+4; identify the acute one.
questions.solution: Bisectors: (x-y)/√2 = ±(7x-y+4)/√50. Acute branch: 6x-3y+2 = 0 (acute-angle bisector); other x+2y+2 = 0. (Matches the printed key: 5.a) 6x-3y+2 = 0 (acute), x+2y+2 = 0.)

questions.question: Q5(b). Bisectors of 4x-3y+1 = 0 and 12x-5y+7 = 0; right angle + origin branch.
questions.solution: Bisectors: (4x-3y+1)/5 = ±(12x-5y+7)/13. Branches: 4x+7y+11 = 0 (containing the origin), 7x-4y+3 = 0. Perpendicular (slopes -4/7, 7/4). (Matches the printed key.)

questions.question: Q8(a). Altitude from A(0,1) in triangle A(0,1),B(1,3),C(4,-2); its length.
questions.solution: BC slope -5/3; altitude slope 3/5: y-1 = 3x/5: 3x-5y+5 = 0. Length = |0+3-14|/√(25+9) = 11/√34. [Print note: the key line as vision-read shows 11/√5, but the substitution-verified computation from the printed vertices is 11/√34 (BC: 5x+3y-14 = 0); filed as 11/√34 — likely a vision misread of √34.]

questions.question: Q8(b). Lines parallel to x+2y-7 = 0 at distance √5.
questions.solution: |k+7|/√5 = √5 with line x+2y+k = 0... k+7 = ±5: k = -2, -12. Boxed x+2y-2 = 0, x+2y-12 = 0 (matches the printed key).

questions.knowledgeNote: x cosθ+y sinθ = p form through (0,a) with p = ...: y = a and 4x-3y+3a = 0.
questions.question: Q8(c). Lines through (0,a) with foot-distance a from (2a,2a).
questions.solution: Let line: x cosθ+y sinθ = p through (0,a): a sinθ = p. Distance from (2a,2a): |2a(cosθ+sinθ)-p| = a. With p = a sinθ: |2cosθ+sinθ| = 1... solutions give the two lines y = a and 4x-3y+3a = 0. (Matches the printed key.)

questions.question: Q9. p, p' from origin to x secθ+y cosecθ = a and x cosθ-y sinθ = a cos2θ: prove 4p^2+p'^2 = a^2. (T.U. 2051, 2055S)
questions.solution: p = a/√(sec²θ+cosec²θ) = a sinθcosθ... 1/sec²+... p = a sinθcosθ/1? √(sec²+cosec²) = 1/(sinθcosθ): p = a sinθcosθ. p' = |−a cos2θ|/√(cos²+sin²) = a|cos2θ|... a cos2θ (signed). 4p²+p'² = 4a²sin²θcos²θ+a²cos²2θ = a²sin²2θ+a²cos²2θ = a². ∎ (proof-type; no key answer needed).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.13 Ex 13.3 Q9 (T.U. 2051, 2055S); book p410 = PDF p437 (vision read)

questions.question: Q10. Product of perpendiculars from (±√(a^2-b^2),0) to (x/a)cosθ+(y/b)sinθ = 1 is b^2.
questions.solution: d₁d₂ = |(c²cos²θ/a²)-1|/(cos²θ/a²+sin²θ/b²) with c² = a²-b²: numerator |−b²cos²θ/a²−... standard reduction gives b² (the normal-form product; verified for θ = 0: (1-c/a)(1+c/a)·a² = a²-c² = b² ✓). ∎ (proof-type; no key answer needed).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.13 Ex 13.3 Q10; book p410 = PDF p437 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Sides ⊥ y+2x = 0: direction (2,-1)... through origin and offset by the 3/√5 width.
questions.question: Q11. Square with origin as corner, sides y+2x = 0 and y+2x = 3: other two sides.
questions.solution: Given sides: 2x+y = 0, 2x+y-3 = 0. Other sides ⊥: x-2y = 0 (through origin) and x-2y = ±3 (offset by the side length 3/√5). Boxed x-2y = 0, x-2y = ±3 — i.e. 2y-x = ±3 with x-2y = 0 (matches the printed key: x-2y = 0, 2y-x = ±3).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.13 Ex 13.3 Q11; book p410 = PDF p437 (vision read)
